source.title: VisualDAN: Exposing Vulnerabilities in VLMs with Visual-Driven DAN Commands

record.tranche_reason: The study develops and evaluates VisualDAN as a visual jailbreak attack. It does not test whether fine-tuning or getting past initial response tokens causes the safety effects in the claim.
record.gate_note: The reported outcomes concern adversarial-image attacks on VLMs, not fine-tuning model weights, response-position KL, compliant text prefills, suffixes, or decoding changes. Results are recorded under fits_no_version. The study also reports toxicity analyses, benchmark comparisons, and an ablation of toxic-corpus size; these do not test a listed claim version.
record.test_reason: This is an attack paper. It optimizes an adversarial image against affirmative-prefix plus harmful targets, then reports its own method's attack success on VLMs. It does not fine-tune weights, measure per-token KL, localize parameters or deepen alignment. It also tests no compliant-text prefill, adversarial suffix or decoding change, so its numbers are attack-performance results, not a test of whether getting past the opening defeats refusal. The closest point is the Figure 4 ablation, where affirmative-prefix targets ('DAN injection') improve the attack over targets without them. That ablation compares the study's own method variants, and the text gives no readable values.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. VisualDAN embeds DAN-style affirmative-prefix commands in adversarial images and bypasses safeguards in MiniGPT-4, MiniGPT-v2, InstructBLIP and LLaVA. The authors also note that a small amount of toxic corpus amplifies toxic output, and they call for stronger defences against image attacks.
record.recipe_differences: The study optimizes an adversarial image with PGD using query-target pairs containing affirmative prefixes and harmful targets; it does not fine-tune the model or use response-token prefilling.
record.method_sensitivity: Attack success changes with image perturbation strength; the study also reports differences across benchmarks and evaluation judges.

fits_no_version.finding: On MiniGPT-v2, adversarial images trained with affirmative-prefix targets (DAN injection) jailbreak more effectively on Manual-40 than images trained on AdvBench without prefixes (Figure 4). The values cannot be read from the text.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizing an adversarial visual input toward affirmative response openings increases harmful compliance over optimizing toward harmful targets alone.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding more toxic strings to the training corpus raises Perspective toxicity (13.6 to 53.0) while GPT4-Eval success first rises then falls (60 to 85, then 27.5) (Table 6).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Once a VLM is jailbroken by an adversarial image, a small toxic corpus amplifies toxicity, and too much toxic data degrades coherence.

record.problems: The authors note that keyword-based ASR is the least accurate evaluator and that Llama-Guard2 can misclassify some responses. GPT4-Eval was validated only on Manual-40 because of API cost. The paper reports averages over three evaluations but no uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 keyword-based ASR and GPT4-Eval values are omitted to keep the record focused on the two other judges; Table 3's separate toxicity categories and Table 4's per-scenario attack comparisons are omitted. Table 6's toxicity/GPT4-Eval results for varying toxic-corpus sizes are also omitted because they do not test a listed claim version. These are in Tables 1, 3, 4, and 6.

untested.parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples; the model weights are untouched.
No per-token KL or comparison of aligned and base models by response position.
No compliant-text prefill, text suffix or decoding change. The adversarial image is optimized toward affirmative openings, but the study does not isolate the effect of the response opening.
No localization of safety in weights or ranks.
No analysis of why alignment is shallow.

missing.what: DAN-injection ablation: ASR with versus without affirmative-prefix targets, across four evaluators. This is the only result touching on the affirmative opening, and its values are figure-only.

record.verdict_notes: The No Attack baselines in Table 1 come from a single column whose metric is unstated, yet the record reused them across judges and misassigned one value (MiniGPT-4 7B is 30.0). The study cites Qi et al. 2310.03693 only in passing. All rows correctly have versions none. The study is white-box and the authors report limited transferability.

versions.untested_parts: The study trains adversarial images, not safety-trained models on harmful examples.
No benign-data fine-tuning of the model is tested.
No per-token KL divergence or aligned-versus-base response-position comparison is reported.
No compliant response prefill, adversarial suffix, or decoding change is tested; the intervention is an adversarial image.
No safety weights or ranks are localized or edited.
The study does not test why safety training would be shallow.
No training to deepen safety across response positions is tested.
